display.purpose: Hero headline and the closing statement; one per screen.

title-sm.purpose: Step names and short item headings.

figure.purpose: Statistics and scores, tabular, always sourced.

lede.purpose: One or two sentences under a headline, in Slate.

caption.purpose: Sources, footnotes, helper text; never below 13px.

label.purpose: Mono inner-page credential lines and data labels; never an eyebrow.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Linked cards on hover, with a 2px upward move.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Rollout chart and result panel at rest.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Colour and 1-3px moves on buttons, links, rows.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: Client logo strip only; pauses on hover; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: rollout-chart
motion.value: one rollout wave (~2.5s), then a spotlight loop (~6s per function), ease cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)
motion.purpose: Hero illustration only; pauses off screen and in background tabs; finished static state under reduced motion.

patterns.name: x-mark
patterns.purpose: One graphic per screen besides the logo: whole (48-72px) or cropped by a container edge (at most half hidden). Never tiled, rotated, outlined or looped.

patterns.name: field-grid
patterns.value: 64px square, Hairline lines at ≤9%, radial mask to ~60% coverage
patterns.purpose: Behind the hero and the teal band only.

arabic.limits: max one line per screen, two per page; hero, teal band, footer only
arabic.size: 1.1x the paired Latin size, line-height ≥1.5, letter-spacing 0

gradients.purpose: Keeps the teal-to-orange midpoint saturated instead of grey.

narrative.overview:
Xanadu sells AI that actually runs the business, to people who are accountable for it. The system looks like a well-run operations room seen at ten in the morning: bright, quiet and exact, with every instrument readable and nothing decorative competing for attention. Confidence comes from restraint and precision, not from effects. The visitor should feel they're looking at people who have shipped this before.

The page is light, near-white haze with plain white surfaces. Two brand colours do all the signalling: **Xanadu Teal** for structure and calm emphasis, **Signal Orange** for the one action that matters. Type is one family, Geist, set large and tight for statements and plain for reading, with Geist Mono kept for small labels and machine output. Density is generous: one idea per section, short copy, wide margins.

Confirmed rejections: dark or black page grounds, glow and spotlight effects, stock "AI" imagery, the old xanadu.co petrol teal, amber and serif look, and text-heavy heroes.
keyCharacteristics: Light-first: Morning Haze ground, Plain White surfaces, Harbour Ink text; one deep Night Lagoon band closes each page.
Two accents only, each with one job: teal structures, orange acts.
One typeface family, with weight and size doing the hierarchy.
Hairline borders and soft, offset shadows; nothing glows.
Short copy: a headline, one or two sentences, one action.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Teal structures, orange acts. If an element isn't the primary action, the current position, or the logo's X, it isn't orange.

rules.name: The One Shout Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange covers no more than about 5% of any screen: one primary button, one marker, at most one highlighted figure.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: No page or section ground darker than Pale Stone, with one exception: the single Night Lagoon closing band. Harbour Ink appears as text, small fills (choice pills, step dots) and nothing larger.

rules.name: The Two Teals Rule
rules.body: Xanadu Teal for fills and display type; Deep Lagoon for anything a person has to read at body size.

rules.name: The No-Grey-Middle Rule
rules.body: Every gradient interpolates in OKLCH: `linear-gradient(90deg in oklch, <teal>, <orange>)`. Plain sRGB blending turns teal to orange through grey; OKLCH keeps the midpoint saturated (it passes through green and gold).

rules.name: The Short Copy Rule
rules.body: A section is a headline, at most two sentences and one action. If a hero needs a third sentence, the headline isn't finished.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. A mono label may carry an inner page's credential line, or label data, but never sits above a section heading as an eyebrow, and never carries a number like "01 —".

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline tracking stays between -0.04em and -0.03em, and line-height never drops below 0.92. Tighter than that and Geist's counters close.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The hero headline may carry a single accent word in a left-to-right Xanadu Teal to Signal Orange gradient, interpolated in OKLCH ("sticks."). It appears once on the site and nowhere else: no other gradient text, ever.

rules.name: The One Idea Rule
rules.body: Each section carries one idea at one scale. A dense section, such as the assessment, is followed by a quiet one.

rules.name: The Close Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Sections sit close enough that the next heading is in reach. If a gap between sections looks like the page has ended, it is too big.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No radial spotlights, blurred colour blobs or neon edges. Depth comes from a border, a soft offset shadow, or a change of ground.

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: One X graphic per screen, besides the logo. Its power is its rarity.

rules.name: The Quiet Pattern Rule
rules.body: If a pattern is the first thing you notice, it's too strong. Patterns sit behind content, never between the reader and the words.

rules.name: The Pause Rule
rules.body: Only two things loop: the client logo strip, which stops on hover, and the hero rollout chart, which stops off screen. Both rest completely under reduced motion.

dos: **Do** keep every page ground Morning Haze or Plain White; the only exception is one Night Lagoon closing band.
**Do** give each screen one Signal Orange primary action, with Char text.
**Do** use Deep Lagoon (#007C89) for teal text at body size, and Kiln (#C24A00) for small orange text.
**Do** keep sections to a headline, at most two sentences and one action.
**Do** attribute every statistic in a Caption source line, and label every demonstration as an example.
**Do** let motion start from content that is already visible: transform-based entrances, and no fade from zero opacity.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: loops stop and content stays put.
**Do** write every gradient as `linear-gradient(<angle> in oklch, …)`.
donts: **Don't** use dark or black page backgrounds (beyond the one Night Lagoon close), glows, radial spotlights or neon edges.
**Don't** move buttons on hover; colour does the work.
**Don't** use the original xanadu.co petrol teal or amber, or the muted teals of the rejected v2 directions.
**Don't** set body text in Xanadu Teal or Signal Orange; they fail contrast on white.
**Don't** stack section labels above headings, or number them "01 —".
**Don't** use gradient text anywhere except the single hero accent word.
**Don't** tile, rotate or animate the X mark, or show it more than once per screen beyond the logo.
**Don't** ship Arabic before a native speaker has approved it; when it ships, never more than one line per screen.
**Don't** use stock AI imagery (brains, circuits, robots, glowing orbs).
**Don't** add continuous motion anywhere except the client logo strip and the hero rollout chart.
